public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Vaught conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaught_conjecture)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace VaughtConjecture

open FirstOrder.Language

/-- The number of countable models of some L-Theory T up to isomorphism -/
def numberOfCountableModels {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theory) : Cardinal :=
  Cardinal.mk (Quotient (Setoid.comap
    (fun (model : {mt : T.ModelType // Countable mt.Carrier}) ↦
    CategoryTheory.Bundled.mk model.val.Carrier model.val.struc)
    equivSetoid))

/--
The Vaught conjecture states that for a countable language L and a complete L-Theory T
the number of countable models of T (up to isomorphism) is finite, $\aleph_0$ or $2^{\aleph_0}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem vaught_conjecture {L : FirstOrder.Language} (hL : Countable L.Symbols)
                          {T : L.Theory} (hT : T.IsComplete) :
  numberOfCountableModels T ≤ Cardinal.aleph0 ∨ numberOfCountableModels T = Cardinal.continuum
  := by sorry

end VaughtConjecture

reformulations.difference: The source's detailed formulation assumes a complete theory with infinite models and counts models of cardinality exactly ℵ₀. Lean omits the infinite-model assumption and uses numberOfCountableModels, whose Countable predicate also includes finite carriers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A complete theory with an infinite model has no finite models, so the counts coincide in the source's domain. If a consistent complete theory instead has a finite model, every model is isomorphic to that finite model. This remains true for infinite languages: any failure of isomorphism between two finite models is witnessed in a finite sublanguage and hence by a first-order sentence. Thus the additional case has Lean count 1 and satisfies the ≤ ℵ₀ disjunct automatically. Including finite models therefore does not change the conjecture.

reformulations.difference: The elaborated theorem uses independent carrier universes for numberOfCountableModels in its two disjuncts, whereas the source writes one universe-independent model count.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every countable carrier can be transported to any universe using equivShrink, with its first-order structure and theory satisfaction preserved. These transports induce mutually inverse equivalences between the quotients by isomorphism. I proved the resulting lifted cardinal equality, invariance of both the ≤ ℵ₀ and = continuum predicates, and an iff between the actual mixed-universe disjunction and the disjunction counting only Type 0 carriers.
